title: Latency & cost cartography: fall 2026 portrait (draft)
content:
Purpose:
Provide a compact, visual-first (ASCII) map of tradeoffs across model size, quantization, and batching strategies for team review. This is meant as collateral for the Q4 hosting SLA review and for feeding the console cost-optimizer recommendations.

Status: draft — rough numbers from internal microbench harness (region: us-west1), mixed production sampling (canary traffic), and simulated burst replay. Not yet normalized for customer mix.

Summary (one paragraph):
Across the dataset we see consistent per-token unit cost reductions from int8 quantization (~25–35% cost improvement vs fp16) but with a latency tail penalty on high-concurrency spikes. Sessionized batching gives the best p95 for interactive sessions at modest cost overhead; opportunistic windowed batching yields the best long-run tokens/sec but hurts p50 for single-turn requests. Edge routing (us-west-edge) reduces median latency by ~18% vs core but increases cost by 6–10% due to smaller batch efficiency.

Methodology:
- Workloads: 3 synthetic traces: interactive-chat (short-turns, many sessions), long-stream (few sessions, long outputs), bursty-bots (microbursts).
- Models: open-7B, open-13B, open-70B (representative families), each run fp16 and int8 tuned kernels.
- Serving configs: (A) sessionized (keep-alive + small batch windows), (B) windowed (100ms aggregation), (C) opportunistic (fill slots up to 256 tokens).
- Metrics captured: p50/p95/p99 latency (ms), throughput (tokens/sec), cost ($ per 1M tokens), cold-start penalty (ms), observed kv-cache hit-rate where relevant.
- Notes: cost estimated from internal price model (GPU-hour amortized + infra overhead); does not include storage or data-plane egress.

Representative numeric table (aggregated):

Model | Quant | Config     | p50(ms) | p95(ms) | p99(ms) | tps (tok/s) | $/1M toks
------|-------|------------|---------|---------|---------|-------------|-----------
7B    | fp16  | sessionized| 42      | 115     | 240     | 18k         | 18.2      
7B    | int8  | sessionized| 48      | 135     | 290     | 21k         | 13.0      
13B   | fp16  | windowed   | 85      | 210     | 470     | 38k         | 25.9      
13B   | int8  | windowed   | 95      | 255     | 560     | 46k         | 17.8      
70B   | fp16  | opportunistic| 240    | 980     | 2100    | 120k        | 142.0     
70B   | int8  | opportunistic| 280    | 1200    | 2600    | 145k        | 98.5      

Interpretation notes:
- Int8 improves steady-state throughput (tps) and $/1M toks but increases tail latencies under bursty arrival because quantized kernels are less tolerant of preemption and have larger kernel variance. That's visible on p99 for 70B-int8.
- Sessionized config shows the lowest median latency for interactive traces — good candidate for user-facing default for hosted API's chat endpoint.
- Windowed batching is best for background embeddings and long-stream workloads where p50 is less critical.

Textual "sparklines" for p95 latency by config (normalized to 7B-fp16 sessionized = 1.0):
- sessionized: ▁▂▃▄▅▆▇▇▇ (p95 multiplicative: 1.0 -> 1.18 -> 1.35 across 7B->13B->70B)
- windowed: ▂▃▅▆▇▇▇▇▇ (good for throughput, p95 drift moderate)
- opportunistic: ▅▆▇▇▇▇▇▇█ (lowest p50, highest p95 tail under bursts)

ASCII histogram: observed p99 latency distribution (sample: bursty-bots trace, 10k requests):
0-100ms   | ██████████  (27%)
100-300ms | ███████     (18%)
300-700ms | █████        (13%)
700-1500ms| ████         (10%)
1500+ ms  | ████████     (32%)  <-- heavy tail from 70B opportunistic + int8 preemptions

Region vs core delta (us-west-edge vs core compute-pool):
- median latency: edge -18% (good UX), p95: edge -10% (varies with KV cache locality)
- cost: edge +6–10% per 1M tokens (smaller pack efficiency, more nodes)
- recommendation: offer edge routing as opt-in for low-latency tiers (higher cost), default route to core with optional fast-fail fallback to smaller quantized variants under overload.

Key tradeoff sketches (short bullets):
- Quality vs cost: int8 lowers $/token but may increase hallucination risk for some model families (note: quality eval pending INF-3223). Don't auto-quantize for customers with tight quality SLAs without eval hooks.
- Tail risk: large models (70B) amplify tail latency when combined with small-batch, low-concurrency windows. Consider pre-warming or reserving capacity for heavy-tail customers.
- Batching policy: dynamic hybrid (sessionized for interactive, windowed for background) looks promising; we need a policy engine to switch at route-level and degrade gracefully.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Run the same cartography with recent kernel selection changes (PR #482) and compare: INF-3210 assigned.
- Quality gates for auto-quantization: how to integrate eval sets in the rollout pipeline? See INF-3223.
- Cost model sensitivity: these $ estimates assume 70% expected GPU utilization; need alternate columns for 50% and 90% util. Add by Oct 28.

Appendix: quick-run notes (how these numbers were collected):
- Harness: local harness + production canary splitter (10% traffic). Each config executed for 1h steady-state followed by 10-minute induced microburst (5000 rps). 99th percentile measured over entire run.
- KV cache hit-rate: sessionized ~62%, windowed ~22%, opportunistic ~45% (figures vary by trace).
- Cold-start penalty: measured as 2s median for large model cold container spin vs 85ms warm reclaim for smaller guest kernels.

Actionable next steps (two-week sprint):
1) Run kernel-swap experiment across 13B-int8 under induced preemption scenarios (owner: Alex) — target: 10/25.
2) Add cost model columns for 50%/90% GPU util and produce a one-pager for pricing (owner: Diego) — target: 10/28.
3) Draft console recommendation v0: default to sessionized for chat endpoints with opt-in edge routing and int8 suggestion only behind quality gate (owner: Priya) — target: 11/02.

Notes to reviewers: please annotate spots where numbers look off; I expect the 70B-int8 p99 to move when Jeremy's scheduling fix lands. Slack thread: #observability-benchmarks.

-- Priya
